note: The topics of the extra modules 55 to 59, beyond the MOOC: newer Java features (all of them in Java 21) and recursion and linked structures. Records (compact constructors that check and normalize, generated toString and equals, an accessor written by hand, static members, a generic record, nested records, records as HashSet and HashMap keys without printing either, equals on double components with 0.0, -0.0 and NaN and on an array component), a sealed interface with records, a final class, a non-sealed class (and an anonymous subclass of it) and a sealed subinterface, exhaustive switches over it without default (type patterns with when guards and nested record patterns), switch expressions on enums, strings and chars with yield, the old switch statement falling through, a switch on Object with case null, guards, arrays, record patterns and enums, instanceof patterns (with &&, negated and with a record pattern), text blocks (\t, \s, a line joined with a backslash, stripped trailing spaces, escaped triple quotes, the closing delimiter's margin, formatted), stripIndent and translateEscapes, String.format and printf (%8.2f, %-10s, zero padding, signs, hex, octal, grouping, %e, %g, argument indexes), var (also in a lambda's parameters), recursion (a caught StackOverflowError, a recursion 1000 calls deep, memoized Fibonacci, permutations, Hanoi, binary search), a linked list of its own (both ends, removing, reversing, recursion over its nodes, a NullPointerException past its end) with a stack and a queue, and a binary search tree of records (three traversals, levels, height, removing a value with two children, and 800 values added in order: a tree 800 levels deep, walked recursively).
